observation.visible_scene: A sideways-oriented (camera rotated ~90°) view of an industrial shredder with two interlocking toothed metal rotors. A large, light-green/white painted steel drum, already showing rust smudges and surface dents, rests diagonally across the rotor gap. A person in a light shirt and dark shorts with a gloved hand is partly visible at the lower edge, standing beside the machine. Concrete ground and a flat reddish metal plate sit to the right; an 'M.Test' logo is fixed at the top-left corner.
visible_changes: The left edge of the drum (the side pressed against the left rotor) progressively dents and crumples inward over the first ~10 frames, the metal folding into a deep crease.

From roughly the middle of the clip onward, the upper rotor teeth grip the drum's rim and pull it, rotating the body so that the open top folds over and the cylinder collapses into a flattened, curved sheet-like piece.
The drum's overall position shifts toward the upper-left (into the teeth) and its silhouette changes from a full cylinder to a bent, partially flattened shell by the last frame.
The shredder rotors turn continuously (tooth positions change frame-to-frame) while the background, ground, red plate and logo remain fixed, indicating the camera is stationary.
The person at the bottom edge becomes more fully visible from about frame 5 onward and remains standing in place, apparently observing/feeding the drum.
outside_clip_unknowns: The drum is already dented at the first frame, so the initial contact/impact that began the deformation occurred before this excerpt.
The clip ends while the drum is still gripped and only partly flattened, so the final shredding outcome is not shown.
Whether the person is operating controls or merely watching is not determinable from the frames.
uncertain_details: Exact rotation direction/speed of the rotors is hard to confirm from discrete frames.
The precise point at which the drum's top rim first engages the upper teeth is gradual rather than a single clear event.
Material identity of the drum (steel vs. aluminum) is inferred from appearance only.
